findings.title: Existing intercompany BAA does not cover this engagement
findings.explanation: The AtliQ Inc ↔ Pvt Ltd subcontractor BAA (C-044) is scoped to the CareBridge engagement only. If anyone outside AtliQ Inc (Pune team, freelancers) will touch PHI or de-identified data for this client, a new per-engagement subcontractor BAA is needed first.
findings.suggestion: Draft a per-engagement subcontractor BAA (Pune and every freelancer) flowing down the client BAA's restrictions before any data moves.
findings.quote: This Agreement applies to the Engagement Services. Any services Subcontractor performs for Business Associate other than the Engagement Services are governed by the Intercompany Agreement.
findings.precedent: Pranav: 'does the CareBridge setup cover this too?' K: 'should do'. Nobody checked (Harrington huddle, 27 Sep).

findings.title: Requires $5,000,000 cyber cover; AtliQ holds $1M
findings.explanation: Karandeep (Harrington huddle, 27 Sep): 'Our cyber policy is $1M btw'. Signing would put AtliQ in breach on day one.
findings.suggestion: Either negotiate the limit to $1M-2M, or get a quote to raise cover before signing (cost goes into the deal price).
findings.quote: 8.3 **Insurance.** Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S. Dollars ($5,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate, covering notification costs, regulatory defense and penalties, and third-party claims arising from Privacy Events, and shall name Covered…

findings.title: No subcontractor BAA for people who will touch the data
findings.explanation: HIPAA requires the same restrictions to flow down to every subcontractor (Pune team via an intercompany BAA, each freelancer via a subcontractor BAA) before data changes hands.
findings.suggestion: Draft per-engagement subcontractor BAAs (intercompany + each freelancer) mirroring the client BAA, signed before access.
findings.precedent: CareBridge (2025) did this right: NDA + MSA + BAA + intercompany subcontractor BAA.

findings.title: PHI must stay in the US — check who already has the data
findings.explanation: This draft forbids PHI outside the US. The Pune team cannot work on identifiable data for this client.
findings.suggestion: Confirm no PHI has left the US; delete any copies offshore; staff PHI work with named US personnel only.
findings.quote: ** Business Associate shall not, and shall ensure that no Subcontractor shall, access, view, create, receive, maintain, transmit, store or process PHI from or at any location outside the United States, whether directly or by remote access

findings.title: Exhibit B is referenced but not attached
findings.explanation: The contract incorporates a document that is not in this draft, so you would be agreeing to terms you have not seen.
findings.suggestion: Ask for Exhibit B before signing and review it with the main agreement.
findings.quote: 9.3 Covered Entity shall provide PHI to Business Associate only through the secure transfer methods or Client-controlled environments specified in Exhibit B to the Master Services Agreement.

findings.title: Patient data may already be in Pune, before any BAA is signed
findings.explanation: The team notes say a sample extract with what looks like real patient data was forwarded to engineers in Pune. The client's BAA forbids PHI outside the US, and no BAA is signed yet.
findings.suggestion: Stop use of the extract, confirm with the client whether it was PHI, delete offshore copies and record it; assess breach-notification duties with US counsel (Calloway Stern).
findings.quote: Pranav: scoping is going well. Kevin Brooks (their data eng manager) emailed a "sample extract" on 12 Sep so we could size the pipeline. Pranav opened it here and forwarded to Sneha and Vikram in Pune to start profiling. "It's real data I think — names, DOBs, some diagnosis codes."

findings.title: Broad one-way indemnity
findings.explanation: One party indemnifies for anything 'arising out of or relating to' the services, while the other side's indemnity (if any) is narrow.
findings.suggestion: Narrow to third-party claims caused by the indemnifying party's breach, negligence or IP infringement, and make it mutual.

context_notes.name: 2026-09-22_internal_contract_queue.md
context_notes.body:
# Internal — contract queue (ad-hoc, 22 Sep)
Present: Karandeep, Bhavin, Dhaval, Jay

Called because three people chased Karandeep on the same morning.

Queue as of today (from Jay's list on the whiteboard):
- Harrington (Dhaval) — $210k, US, their paper — by **1 Oct**
- Lakeshore (Jay) — $64k, US — by **3 Oct**
- BlueOrchid pilot (Jay) — $38k — by **5 Oct**
- Gulf Crown (Bhavin) — $140k, Saudi — by **10 Oct**
- TravelHub (Karandeep) — $52k, Dubai — no date
- Rheinwerk (Bhavin) — €88k, Munich — draft arriving tomorrow, by **15 Oct**
- Sunrise SOW-2 (Dhaval) — $45k — Meera sending this week, wants by **8 Oct**

Discussion:
- Karandeep: reviewing late at night after calls, 10pm onwards. A client-paper MSA takes him 3–4 hrs properly. "Harrington alone is a whole evening and I haven't started."
- Dhaval raised ShopSwift — SOW sat 9 days in July waiting for review, Elena's budget slipped a quarter. "We lost that one to our own queue."
- Volume: Bhavin reckons last year was ~5 contracts/month, this year ~9 (MSAs, SOWs, NDAs, DPAs, amendments). Only Karandeep signs.
- Went through Gulf Crown headline terms. Midway Karandeep stopped: "didn't we sign something with the Dubai hotel people that stops us doing hotels in the Gulf?"
- Nobody could find the Al Noor contract quickly — Dhaval searched the shared drive, not there. Karandeep thinks it's in his email "somewhere".
- Bhavin: "I think that expired, no? It was a 2025 thing." Karandeep not sure.
- Jay: "is there a list of what we've agreed to not do?" — silence.
- Dhaval asked if we should send Harrington to counsel. Karandeep: "it's $210k, but Mehta Rao takes a week." Not decided.
- Bhavin: Gulf Crown can't slip, Faisal has a summit on the 14th.

Karandeep will go through them this weekend.

*(No owner, order of review, or deadline per contract was agreed. The Al Noor contract was not located during the meeting.)*

context_notes.name: 2026-09-27_harrington_huddle.md
context_notes.body:
# Harrington — quick huddle (Sun 27 Sep, call)
Present: Karandeep, Dhaval, Pranav

- Harrington now = 3 docs: NDA (signed Aug), MSA (their paper, in review), BAA (arrived 16 Sep — Rebecca wants it signed together with the MSA). Dhaval: "one more doc for Harrington."
- Pranav: scoping is going well. Kevin Brooks (their data eng manager) emailed a "sample extract" on 12 Sep so we could size the pipeline. Pranav opened it here and forwarded to Sneha and Vikram in Pune to start profiling. "It's real data I think — names, DOBs, some diagnosis codes."
- Dhaval: the BAA says nobody outside the US touches patient data, so he's bringing in Daniel Ortiz, freelance data engineer in Austin. Contractor agreement + NDA drafted on our US template. "US-based, so the offshore thing is solved."
- Karandeep: "Our cyber policy is $1M btw, Harrington BAA wants 5."
- Pranav asked if the CareBridge setup (the intercompany thing) covers this too — Karandeep: "should do, same kind of work." Nobody checked.
- Dhaval: Rebecca needs MSA + BAA by 1 Oct.

Let's talk Monday.

*(No decisions were made. As of 2026-09-28 no Business Associate Agreement had been signed with Harrington; the sample extract remained with the two Pune engineers; no subcontractor BAA had been drafted for Daniel Ortiz; the insurance gap was not raised with Harrington.)*
